old_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene of an osprey, a large bird of prey, in action near a body of water. The bird is seen plunging its head and neck into the water with its wings spread wide, creating a splash as it submerges. The osprey's body is partially submerged, and its head is angled downward during the dive. The background features a natural setting with grasses and reeds, suggesting a wetland or coastal environment. The water is disturbed by the bird's dive, with significant splashes and ripples. The osprey's feathers are a mix of brown and white, blending well with the surrounding environment. The bird then begins to pull its head and neck out of the water, with wings spread wide to maintain balance and control during the emergence.

caption: The video captures an osprey partly submerged in calm water, seen in close side view against a blurred green-and-tan grassy bank. The bird faces left, its white head bearing a dark eye-stripe and yellow eye. A fan of droplets sprays continuously at its rear on the right of frame. At the start one wing is raised high toward the upper right, its primaries splaying as the wing turns more vertical. That wing then sweeps forward and down across the back, lowering the body until the head is partly hidden behind dark feathers. Afterward the bird is more level, the head reappears facing left, and the spread wings extend toward the left while the splash persists. In the final stretch the head drops behind the shoulder as the spread wings stay low and horizontal. Throughout, the barred brown upper-wing feathers remain visible, and the clip ends with the osprey still moving in the water.

draft_caption: The video captures an osprey partly submerged in calm water, seen in close side view against a blurred green-and-tan grassy bank. The bird faces left, its white head bearing a dark eye-stripe and yellow eye. A fan of droplets sprays continuously around its rear at the right of frame. At the start one wing is raised high toward the upper right, its primaries splaying as the tip drifts upward over the first second. That wing then rotates forward and down across the back, pitching the body lower until the head dips partly behind the dark feathers. Afterward the bird levels out, the head reappears facing left, and both wings extend sideways toward the left while the splash persists. In the final stretch the body tilts again with its rear toward the spray, the head dropping behind the shoulder as the spread wing stays low and horizontal. Throughout, the barred brown upper-wing feathers and white underparts remain visible, and the clip ends with the osprey still working in the water.
